text: Andromeda is a nearby large galaxy approaching the Milky Way at about 110 km/s along our line of sight. (a) Explain how astronomers determine this motion using a spectrum. [2] (b) Why is its direction different from the general distant-galaxy trend? [1]
html: Andromeda is a nearby large galaxy approaching the Milky Way at about 110 km/s along our line of sight. (a) Explain how astronomers determine this motion using a spectrum. [2] (b) Why is its direction different from the general distant-galaxy trend? [1]
answerHtml:
Worked solution

(a) Compare stellar absorption lines in Andromeda with laboratory wavelengths. [1] Their shift to shorter wavelengths is blueshift, indicating approach; the fractional shift yields the line-of-sight velocity. [1]

(b) Most distant galaxies recede with cosmic expansion, whereas Andromeda’s local gravitational motion is toward the Milky Way. [1]

Marking guidance

editorialNote: Corrected key redshift to blueshift, and nearest neighbouring galaxy to nearby large galaxy.
